variants.title: Calculate database traffic
variants.context: A cache hit serves a read from the cached copy; a miss goes to the database. Assume each miss causes exactly one database read.
variants.prompt: There are 1000 reads/second and the cache hit rate is 80%. How many reads/second reach the database?
variants.hint: Only the misses reach the database.

mistakes.feedback: That is the number of hits, which the database never sees.
The cache absorbs four fifths of these reads.

variants.title: Calculate database traffic
variants.context: A cache hit serves a read from the cached copy; a miss goes to the database. Assume each miss causes exactly one database read.
variants.prompt: There are 2400 reads/second and the cache hit rate is 75%. How many reads/second reach the database?
variants.hint: Only the misses reach the database.

mistakes.feedback: That is the number of hits rather than the misses.
Three quarters of these reads never reach the database.

variants.title: Calculate database traffic
variants.context: A cache hit serves a read from the cached copy; a miss goes to the database. Assume each miss causes exactly one database read.
variants.prompt: There are 1500 reads/second and the cache hit rate is 60%. How many reads/second reach the database?
variants.hint: Only the misses reach the database.
variants.explanation: 1500 x (1 - 0.60) = 600 reads/second, the same database load as a larger but warmer workload.

mistakes.feedback: That is the number of hits, not the misses.
Multiply by the miss rate, which is 40% here.

variants.title: Handle a cache miss
variants.context: Cache-aside means the application checks the cache itself and fills it from durable storage on a miss. The database stays the source of truth.
variants.prompt: A request finds no cache entry and the database holds the value. The application waits for the cache write before responding. Put the actions in order.

items.text: Store a copy in the cache.
Read the value from the database.
Return the value to the client.

variants.hint: You cannot cache a value you have not retrieved yet.
variants.explanation: Fetch the missing value, populate the cache, then answer. A miss does not mean the durable record is absent.

variants.title: Handle a cache miss
variants.context: Cache-aside means the application checks the cache itself and fills it from durable storage on a miss. The database stays the source of truth.
variants.prompt: This time the cache already holds the value for the key. Put the actions in order.

items.text: The cache returns the copy it is holding.
Check the cache for the key.
Return the value to the client.

variants.hint: Ask whether the database has anything to do on this path.
variants.explanation: On a hit the database is never contacted, which is the whole reason for putting a cache in front of it.

variants.title: Handle a cache miss
variants.context: Cache-aside means the application checks the cache itself and fills it from durable storage on a miss. The database stays the source of truth.
variants.prompt: A request misses the cache and the database holds no record for that key at all. Put the actions in order.

items.text: Return a not-found result without caching a value.
Read the key from the database.
The database reports that no record exists.

variants.hint: Think about what there is to store when nothing was found.
variants.explanation: There is no value to cache here, and inventing an entry would hide a record that gets created later.

variants.title: Handle a stale copy
variants.context: A stale cache entry is a copy that no longer matches the source of truth. Invalidation removes the old copy so the next read refills it.
variants.prompt: The database now stores v2 but the cache still holds v1, and reads check the cache first. What prevents the next read returning v1?
options: Delete the updated record from the database.
Leave the old copy until a user complains about it.
Invalidate the cached entry so the next read refills it.
optionFeedback: That destroys the update you just made durable.
Every read until then keeps returning the old value.
The next read misses, fetches v2, and repopulates the cache.
variants.hint: Which action removes the stale copy while keeping the durable update?
variants.explanation: Invalidating on write forces the next read to fetch the current value.

variants.title: Handle a stale copy
variants.context: A stale cache entry is a copy that no longer matches the source of truth. Invalidation removes the old copy so the next read refills it.
variants.prompt: Cached prices carry a 24-hour lifetime, so a price change takes a day to appear. What should change?
options: Invalidate the entry when the price is written, not at expiry.
Raise the lifetime to a week so far fewer reads reach the database.
Keep the lifetime and have support explain the delay to customers.
optionFeedback: The write is the moment the cached copy became wrong.
That makes the window of wrong prices longer, not shorter.
The promise to the user is wrong, not the explanation.
variants.hint: What event actually made the cached copy incorrect?
variants.explanation: Choose the freshness rule from what the product must promise, then size the miss path for it.

variants.title: Handle a stale copy
variants.context: A stale cache entry is a copy that no longer matches the source of truth. Invalidation removes the old copy so the next read refills it.
variants.prompt: A user loses access to a document, but the cached permission decision still says allowed. What does the design owe here?
options: Wait for normal expiry, because permissions change rarely.
Cache permission checks for longer to reduce database load.
Invalidate the cached decision as soon as permissions change.
optionFeedback: Rare changes still have to take effect when they happen.
That lengthens exactly the window which must stay short.
A revoked user keeps access for as long as that copy survives.
variants.hint: What is the cost of being one minute out of date here?
variants.explanation: Bounded staleness is a product decision, and for authorization the acceptable bound is very small.
